questions.prompt: Which statement best describes Home Science as a Grade 10 subject?
options: It applies science and practical skills to improve family and community living
It studies only cooking for hotels
It focuses only on sewing school uniforms
It deals only with decorating houses
questions.correctAnswer: It applies science and practical skills to improve family and community living
questions.explanation: Home Science connects nutrition, clothing, housing, health, consumer choices and resource management to daily life.
questions.subStrandTitle: Meaning and Scope of Home Science
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the role of Home Science in improving personal, family and community wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Which item is most important when handling a hot sufuria in the kitchen?
options: A dry oven glove or folded dry cloth
A wet towel
A plastic ruler
A paper exercise book
questions.correctAnswer: A dry oven glove or folded dry cloth
questions.explanation: Dry insulated material protects hands from heat. Wet cloth conducts heat and can burn the user.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safe practices when using heat during food preparation.

questions.prompt: Which nutrient is mainly needed for growth and repair of body tissues?
options: Protein
Vitamin C
Water
Dietary fibre
questions.correctAnswer: Protein
questions.explanation: Protein helps build and repair body tissues, especially during growth and recovery from illness.
questions.learningOutcome: State the main functions of nutrients in the body.

questions.prompt: Which food is a good local source of carbohydrates?
options: Ugali
Boiled egg
Sukuma wiki
Omena
questions.correctAnswer: Ugali
questions.explanation: Ugali is commonly made from maize flour and mainly supplies carbohydrates for energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify common foods according to their main nutrients.

questions.prompt: Which practice helps prevent food contamination before cooking?
options: Washing hands with soap and clean water
Tasting food with the serving spoon
Keeping raw meat beside cooked rice
Using a cracked chopping board for all foods
questions.correctAnswer: Washing hands with soap and clean water
questions.explanation: Clean hands reduce transfer of germs to food before and during preparation.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify hygiene practices that reduce food contamination.

questions.prompt: Which method preserves food by removing most of its moisture?
options: Drying
Boiling
Grating
Whisking
questions.correctAnswer: Drying
questions.explanation: Drying reduces moisture, making it harder for microorganisms to grow and spoil food.
questions.learningOutcome: Name basic food preservation methods used in the home and community.

questions.prompt: Which fibre is obtained from cotton bolls?
options: Cotton
Nylon
Polyester
Acrylic
questions.correctAnswer: Cotton
questions.explanation: Cotton is a natural plant fibre obtained from the cotton plant.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish natural fibres from manufactured fibres.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a seam in garment construction?
options: To join two or more pieces of fabric
To remove stains from fabric
To measure body temperature
To preserve vegetables
questions.correctAnswer: To join two or more pieces of fabric
questions.explanation: A seam is a line of stitching used to join fabric pieces in clothing construction.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic sewing terms and their uses in garment construction.

questions.prompt: Which laundry symbol usually warns that a garment should not be ironed?
options: An iron symbol crossed out
A circle with the letter P
A square with a line inside
A basin with water
questions.correctAnswer: An iron symbol crossed out
questions.explanation: A crossed-out iron symbol means ironing may damage the garment and should be avoided.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret common care-label symbols for clothing maintenance.

questions.prompt: Which room activity mainly requires good ventilation to remove moisture and odours?
options: Cooking in the kitchen
Reading in a study room
Folding dry clothes
Arranging books on a shelf
questions.correctAnswer: Cooking in the kitchen
questions.explanation: Cooking releases steam, heat and odours, so ventilation helps keep the kitchen safe and comfortable.
questions.learningOutcome: State the importance of ventilation in different rooms of a home.

questions.prompt: Which resource is non-human in household management?
options: Money
Skill
Time
Energy
questions.correctAnswer: Money
questions.explanation: Money is a non-human resource, while skill, time and energy are human resources used in management.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify household resources used to meet family needs.

questions.prompt: What is a budget used for in a household?
options: Planning income and expenditure
Increasing food spoilage
Choosing fabric colour only
Replacing all family rules
questions.correctAnswer: Planning income and expenditure
questions.explanation: A budget helps a family plan how available money will be used for needs, savings and other expenses.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of budgeting in household decision making.

questions.prompt: Which document shows the price, quantity and total cost of goods bought from a shop?
options: Receipt
Recipe
Pattern
Timetable
questions.correctAnswer: Receipt
questions.explanation: A receipt records details of a purchase and can be used to confirm payment or return faulty goods.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify documents used in common consumer transactions.

questions.prompt: Which first-aid action is suitable for a minor clean cut?
options: Wash hands, clean the cut and cover it with a sterile dressing
Rub soil on the cut to stop bleeding
Leave the cut open and share the cloth used
Apply kerosene to the wound
questions.correctAnswer: Wash hands, clean the cut and cover it with a sterile dressing
questions.explanation: Cleaning and covering a minor cut helps control bleeding and reduces infection risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safe first-aid responses for minor household injuries.

questions.prompt: Which value is shown when family members share household tasks fairly?
options: Responsibility
Wastefulness
Neglect
Dishonesty
questions.correctAnswer: Responsibility
questions.explanation: Sharing tasks fairly shows responsibility and supports cooperation in family living.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise values that promote harmonious family living.

questions.prompt: Which term means choosing goods and services wisely to get value for money?
options: Consumer decision making
Food fermentation
Fabric shrinking
Room zoning
questions.correctAnswer: Consumer decision making
questions.explanation: Consumer decision making involves comparing needs, prices, quality and available money before buying.
questions.learningOutcome: Define basic consumer concepts used in everyday purchases.

questions.prompt: Why should raw meat and ready-to-eat foods be kept apart?
options: To prevent cross-contamination
To make both foods cook faster
To increase the smell of food
To reduce the size of the refrigerator
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent cross-contamination
questions.explanation: Raw meat can carry harmful microorganisms that may contaminate foods that will not be cooked again.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ways of preventing contamination during food storage and preparation.

questions.prompt: Which breakfast best shows a balanced meal for a Grade 10 learner?
options: Porridge, boiled egg, banana and clean water
Tea only
Soda and crisps
Plain mandazi only
questions.correctAnswer: Porridge, boiled egg, banana and clean water
questions.explanation: The meal includes energy food, body-building protein, protective fruit and water.
questions.learningOutcome: Select balanced meals using locally available foods.

questions.prompt: Why is dietary fibre important in meals?
options: It helps bowel movement and reduces constipation
It changes water into protein
It makes all foods sweet
It destroys every microorganism in food
questions.correctAnswer: It helps bowel movement and reduces constipation
questions.explanation: Fibre adds bulk to food waste and supports healthy digestion.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of fibre and water in healthy eating.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to reduce loss of vitamin C when cooking vegetables. Which method is best?
options: Cook quickly in little water and avoid overcooking
Soak overnight then boil for one hour
Cut into tiny pieces and keep uncovered all day
Add a lot of baking soda while boiling
questions.correctAnswer: Cook quickly in little water and avoid overcooking
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is easily lost through heat, water and air, so short cooking with little water helps retain it.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply cooking practices that conserve nutrients in vegetables.

questions.prompt: Which cooking method uses hot fat to cook food quickly?
options: Frying
Steaming
Simmering
Baking
questions.correctAnswer: Frying
questions.explanation: Frying cooks food in hot fat or oil, while steaming uses steam and baking uses dry heat in an oven.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate common cooking methods used in food preparation.

questions.prompt: Why should a meal planner consider a family member with diabetes?
options: The meal should manage sugar intake and support health needs
The person must eat only fried foods
The family should avoid all vegetables
The meal should always be skipped
questions.correctAnswer: The meal should manage sugar intake and support health needs
questions.explanation: Meal planning should consider health conditions so that food supports treatment and wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Consider health needs when planning meals for different family members.

questions.prompt: Which sign most clearly shows that fresh fish may be spoiled?
options: Strong unpleasant smell
Clear bright eyes
Firm flesh
Red gills
questions.correctAnswer: Strong unpleasant smell
questions.explanation: Fresh fish should smell mild. A strong unpleasant odour is a warning sign of spoilage.
questions.learningOutcome: Use quality indicators when selecting perishable foods.

questions.prompt: Which storage practice is best for dry cereals such as maize flour or rice?
options: Keep them in clean, dry, covered containers
Store them open on a damp floor
Mix them with detergent to stop insects
Keep them beside leaking water pipes
questions.correctAnswer: Keep them in clean, dry, covered containers
questions.explanation: Dry, covered storage protects cereals from moisture, pests and contamination.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose suitable storage methods for dry foods in the home.

questions.prompt: Why is blanching useful before freezing vegetables?
options: It slows enzyme activity that can spoil colour, flavour and texture
It turns vegetables into flour
It removes all nutrients
It makes freezing unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: It slows enzyme activity that can spoil colour, flavour and texture
questions.explanation: Brief heating before freezing helps maintain vegetable quality during storage.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain preparatory steps used in preserving vegetables.

questions.prompt: Which condition is needed for yeast to raise bread dough well?
options: Warmth, moisture and food from sugar or flour
Very high heat before mixing
A dry airtight cupboard only
Strong disinfectant in the dough
questions.correctAnswer: Warmth, moisture and food from sugar or flour
questions.explanation: Yeast is active in warm, moist conditions and produces carbon dioxide that helps dough rise.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how biological raising agents work in food preparation.

questions.prompt: Why should a buyer compare unit prices when shopping?
options: To identify which pack gives better value for the same quantity
To make the shopping list longer
To avoid reading labels
To choose the brightest package only
questions.correctAnswer: To identify which pack gives better value for the same quantity
questions.explanation: Unit pricing helps compare cost fairly when products have different package sizes.
questions.learningOutcome: Use simple consumer information to compare value for money.

questions.prompt: Which information on a packaged food label helps a consumer avoid expired products?
options: Expiry or best-before date
Brand colour
Picture size
Barcode position
questions.correctAnswer: Expiry or best-before date
questions.explanation: The date mark helps consumers know whether a packaged food is still within its recommended use period.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret label information when buying packaged foods.

questions.prompt: A shop gives a receipt after a learner buys fabric. Why should the receipt be kept?
options: It is proof of purchase if there is a complaint or return
It increases the weight of the fabric
It replaces measurement of the fabric
It changes the fabric colour
questions.correctAnswer: It is proof of purchase if there is a complaint or return
questions.explanation: A receipt supports consumer rights by showing what was bought, when and at what price.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why consumer records are important after a purchase.

questions.prompt: Which factor should be considered first when choosing clothes for a school practical lesson?
options: Safety and suitability for the activity
The most expensive brand
Whether the fabric is imported
Whether the colour hides all stains
questions.correctAnswer: Safety and suitability for the activity
questions.explanation: Clothing for practical work should allow movement and protect the wearer from hazards.
questions.learningOutcome: Select clothing that suits activity, safety and personal needs.

questions.prompt: Why is cotton comfortable for hot weather in many parts of Kenya?
options: It absorbs moisture and allows air movement
It melts easily near heat
It never creases
It is waterproof
questions.correctAnswer: It absorbs moisture and allows air movement
questions.explanation: Cotton absorbs perspiration and is breathable, making it comfortable in warm conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate fibre properties to clothing comfort and use.

questions.prompt: Which tool is most suitable for removing temporary tacking stitches?
options: Seam ripper
Rolling pin
Vegetable peeler
Measuring jug
questions.correctAnswer: Seam ripper
questions.explanation: A seam ripper is designed to cut and remove stitches without damaging fabric when used carefully.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sewing tools and match them to correct uses.

questions.prompt: Why should fabric be pressed during garment construction?
options: To flatten seams and improve the final appearance
To make the needle sharper
To change cotton into polyester
To remove the need for fitting
questions.correctAnswer: To flatten seams and improve the final appearance
questions.explanation: Pressing shapes fabric, sets seams and gives a garment a neat finish.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of pressing while constructing a garment.

questions.prompt: Which stain should be rinsed first with cold water rather than hot water?
options: Fresh blood stain
Wax stain
Mud that has dried completely
Dust on a dry shirt
questions.correctAnswer: Fresh blood stain
questions.explanation: Hot water can set protein stains such as blood, making them harder to remove.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose appropriate first steps for removing common stains.

questions.prompt: Why should coloured clothes be sorted before washing?
options: To reduce colour bleeding onto lighter garments
To make all garments the same size
To remove the need for detergent
To increase creasing
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce colour bleeding onto lighter garments
questions.explanation: Sorting by colour protects light garments from dyes that may run during washing.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply laundry sorting rules to protect garments.

questions.prompt: Which household practice saves water during cleaning?
options: Using a basin instead of leaving a tap running
Washing one spoon under a running tap for several minutes
Ignoring leaking taps
Pouring clean rinse water away immediately when it can be reused
questions.correctAnswer: Using a basin instead of leaving a tap running
questions.explanation: A basin controls the amount of water used and reduces wastage during cleaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Select practical ways to conserve water at home and school.

questions.prompt: Which lighting is most suitable for detailed sewing work?
options: Bright light directed onto the work area
Dim light behind the worker
Flashing decorative lights
No light to reduce electricity use
questions.correctAnswer: Bright light directed onto the work area
questions.explanation: Good task lighting reduces eye strain and helps the learner sew accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Match lighting needs to household activities.

questions.prompt: Why should cleaning chemicals be labelled and stored away from children?
options: To prevent poisoning and wrong use
To make them look expensive
To improve their smell
To turn them into food preservatives
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent poisoning and wrong use
questions.explanation: Clear labels and safe storage reduce accidents from swallowing or misusing chemicals.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety rules for storing household chemicals.

questions.prompt: Which action shows good time management before a practical food lesson?
options: Reading the recipe and assembling ingredients before starting
Starting to cook before washing utensils
Waiting until food burns before checking it
Leaving all preparation to the last minute
questions.correctAnswer: Reading the recipe and assembling ingredients before starting
questions.explanation: Planning and assembling requirements reduces delays and mistakes during practical work.
questions.learningOutcome: Use planning skills to manage time during practical activities.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports respectful communication in a family meeting?
options: Listening without interrupting and responding politely
Laughing at every opinion
Shouting until others agree
Leaving before decisions are made
questions.correctAnswer: Listening without interrupting and responding politely
questions.explanation: Respectful listening helps family members solve problems and make fair decisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify communication habits that promote positive family relationships.

questions.prompt: A family has maize, beans, sukuma wiki and oranges. Which lunch best combines these foods into a balanced meal?
options: Githeri with sukuma wiki and an orange
Plain maize only
Oranges and tea only
Sukuma wiki without any energy food
questions.correctAnswer: Githeri with sukuma wiki and an orange
questions.explanation: Githeri gives energy and protein, sukuma wiki and orange add protective nutrients and fibre.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan balanced meals using locally available foods.

questions.prompt: A teenager who often feels tired is advised to increase iron intake. Which meal choice would best help?
options: Beans, spinach and a fruit rich in vitamin C
White bread with margarine only
Soda and sweets
Plain boiled cassava only
questions.correctAnswer: Beans, spinach and a fruit rich in vitamin C
questions.explanation: Beans and spinach provide iron, while vitamin C improves absorption of non-haem iron from plant foods.
questions.learningOutcome: Select meals that help prevent common nutrient deficiencies.

questions.prompt: Which menu change would best reduce excess saturated fat in a family supper?
options: Replace deep-fried sausages with stewed beans
Add more cooking oil to vegetables
Serve chips with fried meat only
Remove all vegetables and fruits
questions.correctAnswer: Replace deep-fried sausages with stewed beans
questions.explanation: Stewed beans provide protein with less saturated fat than many deep-fried processed meats.
questions.learningOutcome: Modify meals to support healthy eating habits.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best shows why iodine is added to table salt?
options: It helps prevent iodine deficiency disorders such as goitre
It makes salt a complete protein
It removes all need for vegetables
It turns salt into a preservative for every food
questions.correctAnswer: It helps prevent iodine deficiency disorders such as goitre
questions.explanation: Iodine supports thyroid function, and iodised salt helps prevent deficiency where diets lack iodine.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of fortified foods in preventing nutrient deficiencies.

questions.prompt: A recipe requires steaming rather than boiling vegetables. What is the main nutritional advantage of steaming?
options: Less nutrient loss into cooking water
More oil is absorbed
All fibre disappears
Food becomes unsafe to eat
questions.correctAnswer: Less nutrient loss into cooking water
questions.explanation: Steaming keeps food out of large amounts of water, reducing loss of water-soluble nutrients.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare cooking methods in relation to nutrient conservation.

questions.prompt: A learner prepares chapati dough that is too sticky to roll. What is the best first correction?
options: Add small amounts of flour while kneading until workable
Pour in a full cup of water
Heat the dough before kneading
Add detergent to reduce stickiness
questions.correctAnswer: Add small amounts of flour while kneading until workable
questions.explanation: Adding flour gradually adjusts consistency without making the dough too dry.
questions.learningOutcome: Adjust preparation techniques to achieve suitable dough consistency.

questions.prompt: During meal service, why should hot foods be kept hot until serving?
options: To reduce the time food spends in the danger zone for bacterial growth
To make plates heavier
To remove the need for handwashing
To make all foods taste salty
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce the time food spends in the danger zone for bacterial growth
questions.explanation: Keeping hot foods hot limits bacterial multiplication before the meal is eaten.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply temperature control principles during food service.

questions.prompt: Which pair best matches a preservation method with the principle behind it?
options: Salting - draws water out of food and microorganisms
Drying - adds more moisture to food
Freezing - cooks food completely
Fermentation - removes all microorganisms instantly
questions.correctAnswer: Salting - draws water out of food and microorganisms
questions.explanation: Salt reduces available moisture, making conditions less favourable for spoilage organisms.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate food preservation methods to their scientific principles.

questions.prompt: A family preserves mangoes by making jam. Why is sugar important in jam making?
options: It helps preservation by reducing available water and improves flavour
It changes fruit into protein
It replaces clean jars
It prevents heating from being needed at any stage
questions.correctAnswer: It helps preservation by reducing available water and improves flavour
questions.explanation: High sugar concentration reduces water available for microorganisms and contributes to jam texture and taste.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the function of sugar in preserving fruit products.

questions.prompt: Which step is most important before reusing glass jars for preserved food?
options: Wash and sterilise the jars properly
Wipe only the outside of the jars
Use jars with cracked rims
Fill jars while they are still dirty
questions.correctAnswer: Wash and sterilise the jars properly
questions.explanation: Clean, sterilised jars reduce contamination and help preserved foods keep safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply hygiene procedures when packaging preserved foods.

questions.prompt: A learner has KES 500 to buy ingredients for a balanced supper. Which buying decision is most economical and nutritious?
options: Buy maize flour, beans, vegetables and fruit within the budget
Spend all money on soda and biscuits
Buy only imported snacks for status
Buy meat only and ignore other food groups
questions.correctAnswer: Buy maize flour, beans, vegetables and fruit within the budget
questions.explanation: The choice covers several food groups while respecting the available amount of money.
questions.learningOutcome: Make budget-conscious food choices that support balanced meals.

questions.prompt: Two brands of flour have the same quality. Brand A is 2 kg for KES 220 and Brand B is 1 kg for KES 120. Which is cheaper per kilogram?
options: Brand A
Brand B
They cost the same per kilogram
There is not enough information to compare
questions.correctAnswer: Brand A
questions.explanation: Brand A costs KES 110 per kilogram, while Brand B costs KES 120 per kilogram.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate and compare unit prices for household purchases.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows a consumer responsibility when a product is faulty?
options: Report the fault politely with proof of purchase
Destroy the shop display
Spread false claims without checking facts
Use the product dangerously to test it further
questions.correctAnswer: Report the fault politely with proof of purchase
questions.explanation: Consumers should seek redress responsibly by using evidence and clear communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate responsible ways of seeking redress as a consumer.

questions.prompt: Which label detail helps a person with a peanut allergy most directly?
options: Ingredient list and allergen warning
Package colour
Advert slogan
Shop shelf number
questions.correctAnswer: Ingredient list and allergen warning
questions.explanation: Ingredients and allergen warnings help consumers avoid foods that may trigger allergic reactions.
questions.learningOutcome: Use product-label information to make safe consumer choices.

questions.prompt: A learner is choosing fabric for an apron used in food practicals. Which property is most important?
options: Durable, washable and comfortable fabric
Fabric that melts easily near heat
Very loose net fabric
Fabric that cannot absorb any moisture
questions.correctAnswer: Durable, washable and comfortable fabric
questions.explanation: An apron for practical work should withstand washing, protect clothing and remain comfortable.
questions.learningOutcome: Select fabrics according to intended garment use and care needs.

questions.prompt: Which fibre property makes polyester useful for a rain jacket but less comfortable in very hot weather?
options: It absorbs little moisture
It burns like paper
It is always produced by animals
It dissolves in cold water
questions.correctAnswer: It absorbs little moisture
questions.explanation: Low absorbency can help repel moisture, but it may trap perspiration and reduce comfort in heat.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate manufactured-fibre properties to clothing performance.

questions.prompt: Why is taking accurate body measurements important before cutting fabric?
options: It helps the garment fit well and reduces fabric wastage
It makes sewing needles unnecessary
It changes the fabric fibre content
It removes the need for seams
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the garment fit well and reduces fabric wastage
questions.explanation: Accurate measurements guide pattern choice, layout and cutting for a better-fitting garment.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of accurate measurements in garment construction.

questions.prompt: A seam puckers after machine stitching. Which cause is most likely?
options: Incorrect thread tension or stitch length
Fabric was measured in centimetres
The garment has a care label
The scissors were stored closed
questions.correctAnswer: Incorrect thread tension or stitch length
questions.explanation: Poor tension or unsuitable stitch length can pull fabric unevenly and cause puckering.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify causes of common stitching faults and ways to improve seam quality.

questions.prompt: Which fastening is most suitable where a garment opening needs to close securely and open quickly?
options: Zip fastener
Permanent seam
Tailor tack
Hem allowance
questions.correctAnswer: Zip fastener
questions.explanation: A zip fastener opens and closes a garment opening quickly while holding it securely.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose suitable fastenings for different garment openings.

questions.prompt: Which order is best when laundering a washable school shirt by hand?
options: Sort, mend if needed, soak or wash, rinse, dry and iron as required
Iron, soil, wash without rinsing, then store wet
Dry, wash, stain, rinse and crumple
Soak with coloured clothes, skip rinsing and pack damp
questions.correctAnswer: Sort, mend if needed, soak or wash, rinse, dry and iron as required
questions.explanation: Laundry should follow a logical order that protects garments and ensures cleanliness.
questions.learningOutcome: Sequence appropriate steps in laundering washable garments.

questions.prompt: Why should a stain be treated as soon as possible?
options: Fresh stains are usually easier to remove before they set
All stains disappear if ignored
Old stains always become safer
Treatment makes fabric dirty
questions.correctAnswer: Fresh stains are usually easier to remove before they set
questions.explanation: Prompt treatment prevents many stains from bonding strongly with fibres.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of prompt stain treatment in clothing care.

questions.prompt: A woollen sweater label says dry flat. Why is hanging it on a line risky?
options: The weight of water may stretch it out of shape
It will become waterproof
It will change into cotton
It will remove all warmth permanently
questions.correctAnswer: The weight of water may stretch it out of shape
questions.explanation: Wet wool can stretch when hung, so drying flat helps maintain shape.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply care-label instructions to maintain garment shape and quality.

questions.prompt: Which arrangement best improves workflow in a small kitchen?
options: Place storage, preparation and cooking areas in a logical sequence
Keep cooking fuel next to curtains
Store utensils far from where they are used
Block the doorway with boxes
questions.correctAnswer: Place storage, preparation and cooking areas in a logical sequence
questions.explanation: Good layout reduces unnecessary movement and improves safety and efficiency.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan kitchen spaces for safe and efficient work flow.

questions.prompt: Which colour scheme would make a small dark room appear lighter and more spacious?
options: Light colours with adequate natural or artificial lighting
Very dark colours on every surface
No window covering and no light source
Crowding the room with large dark furniture
questions.correctAnswer: Light colours with adequate natural or artificial lighting
questions.explanation: Light colours reflect more light and can visually enlarge a small room.
questions.learningOutcome: Use colour and lighting principles to improve room appearance.

questions.prompt: Which choice best supports safety when arranging furniture in a living room?
options: Leave clear pathways for movement
Place stools in doorways
Put sharp-edged furniture across walkways
Trail electric cables across the floor
questions.correctAnswer: Leave clear pathways for movement
questions.explanation: Clear pathways reduce trips and make movement safer for all household members.
questions.learningOutcome: Arrange furniture to support safety, comfort and function.

questions.prompt: Which cleaning method is most suitable for removing loose dust from a wooden table before polishing?
options: Dust with a soft dry or slightly damp cloth
Scrub with coarse sand
Pour water and leave it standing
Use a sharp knife to scrape the whole surface
questions.correctAnswer: Dust with a soft dry or slightly damp cloth
questions.explanation: Gentle dusting removes loose dirt without scratching or soaking the wood.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose cleaning methods that protect household surfaces.

questions.prompt: Which practice reduces household energy use when cooking beans?
options: Soak the beans before cooking and use a lid
Cook in an uncovered pot from dry state
Keep opening the pot every minute
Use a very small pot that overflows
questions.correctAnswer: Soak the beans before cooking and use a lid
questions.explanation: Soaking shortens cooking time, and a lid reduces heat loss.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply practical energy-saving methods during food preparation.

questions.prompt: Which waste-management action best follows the reduce, reuse, recycle idea?
options: Use a clean container again before sending it for recycling
Burn all plastic waste in the compound
Mix food waste with broken glass
Buy many disposable items for one event
questions.correctAnswer: Use a clean container again before sending it for recycling
questions.explanation: Reusing extends a product's life, and recycling recovers material after reuse is no longer practical.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply sustainable waste-management practices in the home and school.

questions.prompt: Which action is best when a person gets a minor burn from steam?
options: Cool the burn under clean running water and seek help if severe
Apply cooking oil immediately
Break any blisters with a pin
Cover it with dirty cloth
questions.correctAnswer: Cool the burn under clean running water and seek help if severe
questions.explanation: Cooling a minor burn reduces heat damage. Severe burns need medical attention.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe first-aid responses for common household burns.

questions.prompt: A family wants to start a small snack business. Which first step is most sensible?
options: Identify customer needs, costs and hygiene requirements
Borrow money before deciding what to sell
Cook large amounts without testing demand
Ignore packaging and food safety
questions.correctAnswer: Identify customer needs, costs and hygiene requirements
questions.explanation: A simple feasibility check helps the family plan a safe and realistic enterprise.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan basic steps for a small Home Science related enterprise.

questions.prompt: A learner plans lunch for a construction worker and a younger sibling. Which factor best explains why the worker may need a larger energy portion?
options: The worker does more physically demanding activity
The worker is older so all nutrients are unnecessary
The sibling should avoid all carbohydrates
Energy needs are identical for every person
questions.correctAnswer: The worker does more physically demanding activity
questions.explanation: Energy needs vary with activity level, age, body size and health status.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse factors that influence meal planning for different individuals.

questions.prompt: A family eats mostly refined maize meal, tea and sugar. Which nutrition risk is most likely if this pattern continues?
options: Poor intake of protein, vitamins, minerals and fibre
Excess intake of all protective foods
Too much dietary fibre
Complete balanced nutrition
questions.correctAnswer: Poor intake of protein, vitamins, minerals and fibre
questions.explanation: A diet dominated by refined starch and sugar lacks enough body-building and protective nutrients.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse meal patterns and identify possible nutrient gaps.

questions.prompt: Why is exclusive use of charcoal for indoor cooking a health and safety concern?
options: It can produce harmful smoke and carbon monoxide if ventilation is poor
It always makes food poisonous immediately
It removes all nutrients from food
It prevents all fire risks
questions.correctAnswer: It can produce harmful smoke and carbon monoxide if ventilation is poor
questions.explanation: Poorly ventilated combustion can expose people to smoke and carbon monoxide, which are dangerous.
questions.subStrandTitle: Fuel Safety and Indoor Air Quality
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse health risks linked to household fuels and ventilation.

questions.prompt: A preserved bottle of juice has a swollen cap and gas bubbles before opening. What is the safest decision?
options: Do not drink it because spoilage or unsafe fermentation may have occurred
Shake it and serve to visitors
Boil the sealed bottle on high heat
Mix it with fresh juice to hide the change
questions.correctAnswer: Do not drink it because spoilage or unsafe fermentation may have occurred
questions.explanation: Gas and swelling can indicate microbial activity, so the product should be rejected for safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate preserved foods for signs of spoilage and safety risks.

questions.prompt: Which response best handles a suspected food poisoning incident after a school event?
options: Stop serving the food, preserve a sample if possible and seek medical/public health advice
Continue serving until all food is finished
Throw away all evidence and blame one learner
Treat everyone with random medicines from home
questions.correctAnswer: Stop serving the food, preserve a sample if possible and seek medical/public health advice
questions.explanation: Stopping service protects others, while samples and medical advice support proper investigation and care.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse appropriate actions during suspected foodborne illness.

questions.prompt: A buyer sees cooking oil labelled 2 litres but suspects the seal is broken. Which choice best protects the consumer?
options: Reject it and choose a properly sealed product
Buy it because broken seals reduce price
Taste it in the shop to check quality
Ignore the seal if the label is colourful
questions.correctAnswer: Reject it and choose a properly sealed product
questions.explanation: A broken seal may indicate tampering or contamination, so the safer consumer choice is to reject it.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate product condition before purchase to protect consumer health.

questions.prompt: A household income falls, but the family still needs nutritious meals. Which strategy is most appropriate?
options: Plan menus around affordable local foods such as legumes, grains and seasonal vegetables
Stop planning meals completely
Buy expensive convenience foods daily
Remove all protein foods from the diet
questions.correctAnswer: Plan menus around affordable local foods such as legumes, grains and seasonal vegetables
questions.explanation: Local seasonal foods and legumes can provide good nutrition at lower cost when meals are planned well.
questions.learningOutcome: Adapt household food choices to changing income while maintaining nutrition.

questions.prompt: Which advertising claim should a critical consumer question most?
options: This drink cures every disease in one day
This packet contains 1 kg of flour
Keep refrigerated after opening
Made from maize and millet
questions.correctAnswer: This drink cures every disease in one day
questions.explanation: Extreme health claims are likely misleading and should be checked against reliable evidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse advertising claims and identify misleading information.

questions.prompt: A learner wants a fabric for reusable shopping bags. Which choice is most suitable?
options: Strong woven cotton or canvas
Delicate lace
Very thin tissue fabric
Loose net used for decoration
questions.correctAnswer: Strong woven cotton or canvas
questions.explanation: Reusable bags need fabric that can carry weight, withstand repeated use and be cleaned.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate fabric suitability for functional textile articles.

questions.prompt: Why is it risky to cut fabric before checking the grain line?
options: The finished garment may twist, hang poorly or lose shape
The fabric will become heavier
The sewing machine will stop working permanently
The thread will change colour
questions.correctAnswer: The finished garment may twist, hang poorly or lose shape
questions.explanation: Correct grain placement helps a garment hang and fit as intended.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the effect of grain line on garment quality.

questions.prompt: A school shirt has a missing button and a small tear. Which decision best extends its useful life?
options: Repair the tear and replace the button before laundering and wearing
Throw it away immediately
Hide the tear with wet chalk
Wash harder until the tear disappears
questions.correctAnswer: Repair the tear and replace the button before laundering and wearing
questions.explanation: Timely mending prevents further damage and supports economical clothing management.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate repair options that extend garment life.

questions.prompt: Which laundry mistake is most likely to shrink or damage a wool garment?
options: Washing roughly in hot water and drying with high heat
Drying flat in shade
Using mild detergent as directed
Following the care label
questions.correctAnswer: Washing roughly in hot water and drying with high heat
questions.explanation: Heat and agitation can cause wool fibres to felt, shrink or lose shape.
questions.subStrandTitle: Care of Wool and Delicate Fabrics
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse causes of damage in delicate garments during laundry.

questions.prompt: A room is noisy, crowded and poorly lit for studying. Which improvement addresses function most directly?
options: Create a quiet, well-lit study corner with only necessary furniture
Add more decorative cushions only
Paint one wall a bright colour and keep clutter
Move the study table next to a loud television
questions.correctAnswer: Create a quiet, well-lit study corner with only necessary furniture
questions.explanation: Function improves when the room arrangement supports the activity, comfort and concentration.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate room arrangements according to user needs and activities.

questions.prompt: Which design decision best supports accessibility for an elderly person at home?
options: Keep floors uncluttered and provide stable seating with good lighting
Use slippery mats in walkways
Store daily items on the highest shelf
Remove hand support from stairs
questions.correctAnswer: Keep floors uncluttered and provide stable seating with good lighting
questions.explanation: Clear, well-lit spaces and stable furniture reduce falls and support independence.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse home design choices that support safety for different users.

questions.prompt: A household wants to reduce dampness and mould in a bedroom. Which combined action is best?
options: Improve ventilation, allow sunlight where possible and fix water leaks
Close windows permanently and dry wet clothes indoors
Paint over mould without removing moisture sources
Place more furniture against damp walls
questions.correctAnswer: Improve ventilation, allow sunlight where possible and fix water leaks
questions.explanation: Mould control requires reducing moisture and improving air circulation, not just covering stains.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate ways to maintain healthy indoor conditions.

questions.prompt: Which household plan best manages scarce water during a dry period?
options: Prioritise safe drinking, cooking and hygiene, then reuse grey water where safe
Use clean drinking water to wash the compound first
Stop all handwashing to save water
Store water in open containers without covers
questions.correctAnswer: Prioritise safe drinking, cooking and hygiene, then reuse grey water where safe
questions.explanation: Water management should protect health first and reuse suitable water safely for lower-risk tasks.
questions.learningOutcome: Prioritise household resource use during scarcity.

questions.prompt: A family timetable gives one person all chores while others are free. Which weakness does this show?
options: Unfair workload distribution
Good delegation
Efficient teamwork
Balanced responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: Unfair workload distribution
questions.explanation: A fair duty roster considers age, ability, time and shared responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse household task plans for fairness and efficiency.

questions.prompt: Which response best supports a younger child who refuses to eat vegetables?
options: Offer vegetables in small portions and model eating them calmly
Force a large serving as punishment
Remove all other foods until the child gives in
Tell the child vegetables are medicine only
questions.correctAnswer: Offer vegetables in small portions and model eating them calmly
questions.explanation: Positive modelling and gradual exposure can build acceptance without creating fear around food.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply supportive strategies for healthy habits in children.

questions.prompt: A home-based baker receives complaints that cakes arrive crushed. Which improvement should be made first?
options: Use suitable packaging that protects shape and hygiene during transport
Stop labelling products
Increase sugar in every cake
Ignore customer feedback
questions.correctAnswer: Use suitable packaging that protects shape and hygiene during transport
questions.explanation: Packaging should protect food quality, safety and appearance from production to customer.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse customer feedback to improve a small food enterprise.

questions.prompt: Which record would most help a small tailoring business know whether it is making a profit?
options: A record of costs, sales and cash received
A list of favourite colours only
A drawing of the sewing room
A list of unrelated school subjects
questions.correctAnswer: A record of costs, sales and cash received
questions.explanation: Profit can be estimated only when business costs and income are recorded accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate the importance of records in a small Home Science related enterprise.

questions.prompt: A school wants to run a nutritious low-cost snack project using locally available foods. Which plan is strongest?
options: Test demand, cost ingredients, standardise recipes, maintain hygiene and set a fair selling price
Cook random snacks daily without costing
Buy costly imported ingredients to look modern
Set prices before knowing costs or portion sizes
questions.correctAnswer: Test demand, cost ingredients, standardise recipes, maintain hygiene and set a fair selling price
questions.explanation: A viable food project combines market need, costing, consistent quality, hygiene and realistic pricing.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop a basic plan for a safe and viable Home Science enterprise.

questions.prompt: A family has KES 1,000 for three dinners and wants balanced meals. Which approach is best?
options: Make a three-day menu, buy seasonal foods in planned amounts and use leftovers safely
Buy snacks first and plan meals with what remains
Spend the full amount on meat for one dinner
Avoid comparing prices because planning takes time
questions.correctAnswer: Make a three-day menu, buy seasonal foods in planned amounts and use leftovers safely
questions.explanation: Menu planning, seasonal buying and safe use of leftovers stretch money while maintaining nutrition.
questions.learningOutcome: Create economical meal plans that meet nutrition needs over several days.

questions.prompt: A learner compares boiling, steaming and stir-frying vegetables for a nutrition display. Which conclusion is most accurate?
options: Steaming and quick stir-frying usually conserve more water-soluble nutrients than long boiling
Long boiling always conserves the most vitamin C
All methods have exactly the same nutrient effect
Adding excess water increases every vitamin
questions.correctAnswer: Steaming and quick stir-frying usually conserve more water-soluble nutrients than long boiling
questions.explanation: Short cooking and limited water reduce losses of heat-sensitive and water-soluble nutrients.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate cooking methods for nutrition, texture and safety.

questions.prompt: A preserved tomato sauce keeps spoiling after one week. Which investigation should be done first?
options: Check hygiene, heating time, acidity, container sterilisation and storage temperature
Change the label colour only
Use larger jars without cleaning them
Reduce heating to save fuel regardless of safety
questions.correctAnswer: Check hygiene, heating time, acidity, container sterilisation and storage temperature
questions.explanation: Spoilage can result from contamination, poor heat processing, unsuitable acidity or poor storage.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate causes of failure in preserved food products.

questions.prompt: A consumer group suspects a shop uses false weighing scales. Which action is most responsible?
options: Gather evidence and report to the relevant consumer or standards authority
Damage the shop property
Post insults online without evidence
Continue buying silently and warn nobody
questions.correctAnswer: Gather evidence and report to the relevant consumer or standards authority
questions.explanation: Consumer protection works best through evidence, lawful reporting and responsible communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Propose responsible action for suspected unfair trade practices.

questions.prompt: A learner is designing a simple garment for a child. Which set of choices best supports safety and comfort?
options: Soft washable fabric, secure fastenings and no loose choking hazards
Scratchy fabric, loose beads and tight neck opening
Heavy fabric that restricts movement
Decorations fixed with sharp pins
questions.correctAnswer: Soft washable fabric, secure fastenings and no loose choking hazards
questions.explanation: Children's garments should be comfortable, easy to care for and free from unsafe loose parts.
questions.learningOutcome: Create garment design choices based on safety, comfort and care requirements.

questions.prompt: A garment business wants to reduce textile waste. Which practice best supports sustainability and profit?
options: Plan pattern layout carefully and turn suitable offcuts into small saleable items
Throw all offcuts into mixed waste
Cut fabric randomly to save thinking time
Buy more fabric than needed for every order
questions.correctAnswer: Plan pattern layout carefully and turn suitable offcuts into small saleable items
questions.explanation: Efficient layout reduces waste, and useful offcuts can become value-added products.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop ways of reducing textile waste in clothing production.

questions.prompt: A small bedsitter must serve as a study, sleeping and cooking space. Which planning principle is most useful?
options: Zone the space by activity while keeping safe circulation and ventilation
Place the cooker next to bedding to save steps
Store books on the cooking surface
Block the window to create privacy at all times
questions.correctAnswer: Zone the space by activity while keeping safe circulation and ventilation
questions.explanation: Zoning separates activities, while circulation and ventilation protect safety and comfort in a small home.
questions.learningOutcome: Create functional layouts for limited household space.

questions.prompt: A household wants a weekly cleaning plan that saves time and protects health. Which plan is best?
options: List tasks by frequency, assign people fairly, include hygiene-critical areas and review supplies
Clean only when visitors are expected
Give all tasks to the youngest child
Use strong chemicals everywhere without reading labels
questions.correctAnswer: List tasks by frequency, assign people fairly, include hygiene-critical areas and review supplies
questions.explanation: A good cleaning plan organises tasks, people, materials and health priorities.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a household work plan that balances hygiene, time and fairness.

questions.prompt: A learner is asked to improve family health through Home Science practices. Which proposal is most comprehensive?
options: Plan balanced meals, safe food handling, clean housing, wise budgeting and shared responsibilities
Buy supplements and ignore meals, hygiene and housing
Decorate the sitting room only
Focus on fashion trends and avoid household safety
questions.correctAnswer: Plan balanced meals, safe food handling, clean housing, wise budgeting and shared responsibilities
questions.explanation: Home Science improves wellbeing through connected decisions about food, safety, housing, resources and relationships.
questions.subStrandTitle: Applying Home Science to Family Wellbeing
questions.learningOutcome: Synthesize Home Science knowledge to improve family health and quality of life.
